category_title: Students with ASD exhibiting out-of-seat and assaultive behavior for attention
minimal_context: Brian is expected to complete his morning academic programmes at his table in the classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Brian, it is time to start our morning lessons. We have five academic programmes to work through at your table today.

STUDENT: (Stands up from his chair and steps away from the table) I don't want to do these.

TUTOR: Please sit back down and try to do the work.

STUDENT: (Walks away from the table and heads toward the classroom door, looking back to see if you are watching)

TUTOR: Brian, you need to come back to your table right now.

STUDENT: (Remains away from the table and shoves a peer who is sitting nearby)

options.A: Guide Brian through a healing-lake visualization at his table, encouraging him to observe the lake carefully and notice that it is always changing, yet always itself.
options.B: Create pictorial descriptions of the morning academic programmes, providing them to Brian to use as he works through his tasks at his table during the session.
options.C: Have Brian complete reflective journal entries at his table, in which he is encouraged to write or draw freely on his experience with the morning academic programmes.
options.D: Add a weekly school-to-home contingency to the behaviour contract, requiring Brian to meet a set number of academic targets per week to access a preferred weekend activity with his family.
